stories.headline: US and Saudi Arabia launch joint airstrikes on Iran-backed militia bases in Iraq
stories.body:
United States and Saudi Arabian military forces have carried out coordinated airstrikes targeting bases of the Popular Mobilisation Forces in Iraq [c1]. The military action follows allegations that the Iran-backed group had previously launched 30 drone strikes against Saudi Arabia [c2]. According to reports, the joint US-Saudi air raids killed at least 20 fighters associated with Iraq's Popular Mobilisation Forces [c6]. The strikes mark a significant escalation in regional conflict across the Middle East.

Hostilities have escalated across several borders in recent days. Satellite imagery from Monday showed that the major Abqaiq oil facility in Saudi Arabia was hit by drones launched by Iranian proxy militias operating from Iraq [c4]. Earlier, on 13 July, Saudi Arabia bombed Sanaa airport outside the capital of Yemen to prevent an Iranian aircraft from landing [c5]. That airport bombing triggered retaliatory strikes by Houthi forces against Saudi airports in Abha and Jizan [c5]. In another major incident, Iran launched missiles at US military installations in Jordan [c7]. This was Iran's first attack in the region following a brief pause in fighting with the US [c7]. Meanwhile, a drone strike hit a US-owned floating storage tanker on Wednesday at a natural gas loading port in Damietta, Egypt [c8]. Commenting on the situation, US President Donald Trump stated that the United States would be "hitting [Iran] hard" [c10].

The air attacks triggered immediate diplomatic consequences in the region. Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi cancelled a scheduled meeting in Jeddah with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman following the US-Saudi military raids [c9]. Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, who is the de facto ruler of Saudi Arabia, previously launched the country's Vision 2030 initiative to diversify the national economy away from its dependence on oil revenues [c3].

The broader regional conflict has also caused severe damage to international shipping and local economies. Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi stated that Egypt lost around $7 billion in 2024 because of a steep decline in shipping traffic through the Suez Canal [c11]. Figures show that annual transit ship counts through the canal halved from over 26,000 vessels down to just over 13,000 [c12]. As a result, annual revenues from the Suez Canal dropped sharply from $10.25 billion in 2023 to around $4 billion in 2024 [c12].

vocab.meaning: planned and executed together in an organized way
done in action to harm someone who harmed you first
military bases or official structures
to expand into new areas to reduce risk or dependence

stories.headline: Wildfires rage across southern Europe during intense summer heatwave
stories.body:
Firefighters across southern Europe are battling severe wildfires driven by high temperatures and strong winds [c13]. In southwest France, a massive wildfire west of Bordeaux burned approximately 420 square kilometers of the Gironde region [c14]. More than 200,000 residents and tourists were forced to flee the flames in the region [c16], though about 57,000 residents from three towns were later allowed to return to their homes [c15]. Local authorities placed French firefighters on high alert [c13], and the Gironde prefecture reported that 126 firefighters have been injured since the blaze began [c20]. The fires have also killed or stranded thousands of wild animals, prompting rescue efforts by volunteers and firefighters [c24].

The crisis extends across the Mediterranean region. In Spain, wildfires have burned over 170 square kilometers, which is six times more area than burned during the same period last year [c17]. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez announced that the government raised the fire near Madrid to "operational level 3" for the first time in Spanish history [c23], noting that the upcoming 12 hours would be critical for containment efforts [c22]. Víctor Resco de Dios, a professor of forestry engineering, warned that the region has entered an era of unextinguishable fires [c18]. In Greece, three firefighters died while fighting blazes on Crete and the southern mainland [c19]. Across southern Europe, over 330,000 people have been evacuated from homes and hotels [c21].

vocab.meaning: a local government administrative area or district office
the act of keeping something dangerous under control

stories.headline: Powerful earthquake in Japan leaves 18 dead as search operations continue
stories.body:
A powerful earthquake struck the island of Kyushu in southwestern Japan, leaving at least 18 people dead and triggering major emergency responses [c25], [c26]. The Japan Meteorological Agency recorded the Kumamoto quake at a magnitude of 7.1, while the US Geological Survey measured it at 6.8 [c25]. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi stated that emergency teams face a race against time to rescue people trapped in damaged structures [c26]. Prime Minister Takaichi deployed over 4,600 personnel to aid search and rescue operations [c31].

The region experienced over 100 aftershocks following the initial quake on Tuesday [c29], including a 5.8 magnitude aftershock that hit the Amakusa and Ashikita areas around 10:20 pm [c28]. Retail company president Akio Yoshida reported that three employees died and four were hospitalized when an explosion struck the Aeon Mall in Kashima an hour after the earthquake [c30]. Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi announced that about 300 air conditioning units would be flown to Kumamoto to support evacuees facing severe heat [c32]. Widespread structural damage was reported across Kumamoto prefecture, including the collapse of the worship hall at the 19th-century Yatsushiro Shrine [c33]. Industrial operations were also affected; Toyota and Honda suspended factory operations in Kumamoto until Friday [c27]. However, semiconductor manufacturer TSMC resumed work at its local plant on Tuesday evening after passing safety checks [c34]. TSMC established the facility in 2021 with Sony, Denso, and Toyota, targeting over $20 billion in total investment [c35].

vocab.meaning: people who have been moved away from a dangerous place
temporarily stopped or paused

stories.headline: Dr. Anthony Fauci invokes Fifth Amendment during US Senate hearing on COVID-19 origins
stories.body:
Former US official Dr. Anthony Fauci invoked his Fifth Amendment constitutional right to avoid answering questions during a US Senate Homeland Security Committee hearing on the origins of COVID-19 [c36]. The constitutional privilege protects individuals from self-incrimination. In his opening statement, Dr. Fauci criticized committee member Senator Rand Paul, saying the senator had an "obvious obsession" with seeing him behind bars [c40].

The hearing was marked by high political tension and public disputes. Committee Chairman Rand Paul ordered Capitol Police to remove Dr. Fauci's defense attorney, David Schertler, after Schertler spoke without being formally recognized [c42]. Schertler called his removal "outrageous" and described the hearing as biased and baseless [c43]. Senator Josh Hawley mocked Dr. Fauci's decision, stating that taking the Fifth Amendment did not indicate honesty [c44]. President Donald Trump commented on social media during the proceedings, calling Dr. Fauci crazy and accusing him of protecting China [c41]. President Trump later told reporters that Dr. Fauci invoked the right simply because his lawyer told him to [c45]. Meanwhile, Senator Paul announced plans to hold a vote to cite Dr. Fauci for contempt of Congress [c38]. In defense of the doctor, a group of 155 scientists signed an open letter calling for an end to scientist harassment, asserting no credible evidence supported charges against Dr. Fauci [c37]. It was also noted that former President Joe Biden had previously granted Dr. Fauci a pre-emptive pardon covering his actions from 2014 to 2025 [c39].

vocab.meaning: referred to a law or right to support a position
disobedient or disrespectful behavior toward a court or legislative body

stories.headline: Russia files terrorism charges against Telegram founder Pavel Durov
stories.body:
Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) has charged 41-year-old Telegram founder Pavel Durov with aiding terrorism and placed him on an international wanted list [c46]. The FSB alleged that Ukrainian intelligence used a dating chatbot on the messaging platform to recruit Russian citizens for sabotage and terrorism [c47]. Russian authorities reported detaining 46 Telegram users between the ages of 12 and 22 over the past year for alleged involvement in arson, sabotage, and attacks on law enforcement [c48]. Following the announcement, Telegram's official account on X posted an image of Durov making an obscene gesture [c49].

Durov, who holds dual citizenship in France and the United Arab Emirates, currently resides in Dubai [c50]. He previously left Russia in 2014 after refusing government demands to close political opposition groups on his former platform, VKontakte [c52]. In 2024, Durov was arrested in Paris on preliminary charges related to illegal activity on Telegram, including drug trafficking and child abuse material, before returning to Dubai in March 2025 [c51]. In April 2026, Durov revealed that Russian authorities sent a criminal summons for him to a Russian apartment where he had not lived for twenty years [c53].

vocab.meaning: deliberately destroying or damaging something for political or military advantage
an official order to appear in a court of law

stories.headline: Lok Sabha passes new anti-paper leak bill following nationwide student demonstrations
stories.body:
The Lok Sabha has passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, by voice vote amid ongoing opposition protests [c54]. The passage of the bill comes after widespread public outrage and nationwide student demonstrations over exam paper leaks and irregularities in the NEET examination process [c54], [c57]. Opposition members protested in Parliament against recent police actions taken against student protesters during the nationwide demonstrations [c54].

Under the strict provisions of the new legislation, individuals convicted of involvement in public exam paper leaks face 5 to 10 years in prison and fines up to Rs 50 lakh [c55]. Furthermore, individuals found guilty of participating in organized paper-leak crimes will face a minimum sentence of 7 years in prison alongside fines reaching up to Rs 10 crore [c55]. Minister of State Jitendra Singh informed lawmakers that 52 First Information Reports (FIRs) have been registered under anti-paper leak legislation since the original framework took effect in 2024 [c56].

The legislative move follows significant political fallout and civil unrest surrounding national entrance tests. Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan submitted his resignation on July 25 after intense public pressure and student marches [c57]. Demonstrations were spearheaded by youth groups, including the Cockroach Janta Party. Founder Abhijeet Dipke publicly criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi's social media outreach to youth, suggesting the Prime Minister should leave his post to become an online influencer [c58]. Dipke warned that students would initiate an even larger nationwide protest if the government refused to withdraw criminal FIRs filed against student demonstrators [c59].

Key figures involved in the student protests have reported facing political heat and threats. Cockroach Janta Party spokesperson Ratna Singh disclosed on social media that she received abusive messages and death threats following the rallies [c60]. Meanwhile, Abhijeet Dipke returned to his hometown of Sambhajinagar in Maharashtra on July 29 after the conclusion of a 36-day student agitation [c61].

vocab.meaning: specific requirements or rules within a legal document
actions that do not follow official rules or standard procedures
a state of public protest or political unrest
a law or set of laws passed by a parliament

stories.headline: Meta promises enhanced oversight for PM Modi's social media accounts after video removal
stories.body:
Social media giant Meta has sent an official communication to India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology promising enhanced oversight for content posted by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and other public figures [c62]. The action follows an incident where Facebook briefly restricted a July 23 selfie video posted by Prime Minister Modi addressing youth on the NEET paper leak issue due to an automated filtering error [c63]. In the video, Prime Minister Modi assured students that the government would introduce fast-track courts and tougher legislation to combat exam leaks [c67].

India's IT Ministry summoned Meta's global head of public policy regarding the video removal [c66]. IT Secretary S Krishnan stated that although Meta apologized, the government was not satisfied with the company's explanation and requested further details [c64]. Separately, Meta previously scrapped its "Muse Image" AI tool globally after public privacy concerns regarding data scraping from public Instagram accounts [c65]. Meanwhile, law enforcement expanded investigations into social media activity surrounding student protests. The Delhi Police Special Cell registered an FIR against platform X over alleged defamatory posts targeting the Prime Minister [c68], having identified 450 accounts that shared deepfakes and AI content during the protests [c69].

vocab.meaning: the action of monitoring or supervising an activity
damaging to the good reputation of someone

stories.headline: Madhya Pradesh raises moong procurement cap as protesting farmers march on Bhopal
stories.body:
The Madhya Pradesh state government increased its summer moong procurement cap from 25% to 60% of total crop output after nearly 2,000 protesting farmers marched into Bhopal [c70]. Farmers affiliated with the Samyukta Kisan Morcha broke through police barricades to gather at Roshanpura Square, setting up camp within one kilometer of Chief Minister Mohan Yadav's residence [c74]. The protesters arrived in tractor-trolleys stocked with five days of food and water, pledging to stay until all demands were addressed [c76]. In response, Chief Minister Yadav appointed a four-member ministerial committee to conduct formal negotiations [c75].

Farmer leaders pointed out that while the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for summer moong was set at ₹8,768 per quintal for 2026–27, excess crop was selling in open markets for only ₹4,000 to ₹5,000 per quintal [c77]. State Agriculture Minister Aidal Singh Kansana announced the extension of the procurement deadline to August 20 and suspended the MSP e-token system for fertilizer distribution [c72]. Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan confirmed that Madhya Pradesh had procured about 60,000 metric tonnes of moong as of July 29 [c71]. The central government agreed to purchase 4.54 lakh metric tonnes at ₹8,780 per quintal [c73].

vocab.meaning: the process of buying or obtaining goods or supplies
temporary barriers built to block passage

stories.headline: Clashes in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir spark political outrage and diplomatic disputes
stories.body:
Violent clashes between security forces and protesters in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) have resulted in widespread casualties and political tension [c78]. Reports state that over two dozen people were killed when Pakistani security forces opened fire during protests [c78], while local officials and independent estimates cited by The New York Times put the death toll at least 30 between early June and late July [c82]. In response to the violence, National Conference president Dr. Farooq Abdullah urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, and the UN Human Rights Council to intervene [c79].

The unrest comes amid elections for 45 assembly seats, during which Pakistani authorities deployed roughly 2,100 army troops and 18,560 security personnel [c83]. The Joint Awami Action Committee and the local chapter of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf boycotted the vote as a "sham" [c84]. Founded in 2003, the Joint Awami Action Committee has demanded the abolition of 12 assembly seats reserved for refugees living in Pakistan [c80]. UN High Commissioner Volker Türk criticized communications blackouts imposed during the turmoil [c85]. Meanwhile, the Indian Embassy in the US publicly criticized a New York Times headline, insisting the area must be called "Pakistan-occupied Kashmir" [c81].

vocab.meaning: to become involved in a difficult situation to change what happens
the formal ending of a system, practice, or institution

stories.headline: Supreme Court accepts CBI closure report clearing former PM Manmohan Singh
stories.body:
A Supreme Court bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant has accepted the Central Bureau of Investigation's (CBI) closure report clearing former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh in the long-standing coal block allocation case [c86]. The ruling brings a formal end to legal proceedings regarding allegations connected to his time overseeing coal allocations. Former Prime Minister Singh passed away in December 2024 while an appeal against a trial court summons was still pending [c87].

During the hearing, Senior Advocates Kapil Sibal and A.M. Singhvi requested that the Supreme Court set aside adverse remarks made by the trial court against Singh despite his death [c89]. The Supreme Court determined that the trial court special judge lacked valid legal justification when rejecting the CBI's 2014 closure reports, which had originally cleared the former prime minister [c90]. The coal allocation case dates back several years; in August 2014, the Supreme Court had quashed 214 coal block allocations made between 1993 and 2010 after ruling that the allocation processes were arbitrary and illegal [c88].

vocab.meaning: officially rejected or declared void by a court
unfavorable, negative, or harmful

stories.headline: Assam flood death toll rises to 75 as state announces enhanced relief grants
stories.body:
The death toll from severe flooding in Assam has reached 75 following seven new reported fatalities in Sivasagar district [c91]. Despite the rising death toll, overall flood conditions showed slight improvement, with the total number of affected residents falling to 3.32 lakh across 622 villages and 21 revenue circles [c92]. Charaideo remains the hardest-hit district, with approximately 1.42 lakh people impacted by high water levels [c93]. Floodwaters submerged over 45,300 hectares of cropland statewide, while the Dhansiri river continued to flow above its danger mark in Numaligarh district [c98].

Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma announced several emergency relief measures for affected populations. Families in Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat, and Golaghat districts will receive an interim grant of ₹15,000 for immediate household needs [c94]. The state government also increased financial ex-gratia compensation for families of flood victims from ₹4 lakh to ₹9 lakh, adding ₹5 lakh directly from the Chief Minister's Relief Fund [c96]. Rules were simplified by waiving post-mortem requirements, accepting certificates from local circle officers instead [c97]. To maintain communication, telecom authorities activated Intra Circle Roaming in Sivasagar [c95].

vocab.meaning: deaths caused by an accident, disaster, or war
money awarded to someone to make up for loss or suffering
